name: Basilica of the Blessed Virgin of Gethsemani
history: French Trappist monks from the Abbey of Melleray founded Gethsemani on 21 December 1848; it was made an abbey in 1851. Its monastery, modelled on Melleray, was begun in October 1852 with bricks made on site, and the abbey church was consecrated on 15 November 1866. It is the oldest operating Trappist monastery in the United States and the motherhouse of all U.S. Trappist houses.
arch: A long whitewashed abbey church with a tall steeple, in the Kentucky knobs near Bardstown. The bricks were made on the spot; the foundation is Indiana limestone.
features: The monks support themselves by selling fruitcake and bourbon fudge.
Writer Thomas Merton lived here as a monk from 1941 until his death in 1968.

look.d: The steeple marks the abbey in the quiet Kentucky hills.
Trappists live by prayer, work and silence.

fun: In 1851 it was declared the "Proto-Abbey of the New World".
journal: Merton's abbey. Even the sky seems to keep silence here.
